biography.plain_text: Urs Schwarzenbach is a Swiss financier who made his fortune in currency trading. His father supplied initial capital. After banking work in Zurich and London, he established his own dealing business. He later invested in hotels, property and farmland, becoming the majority shareholder and financial backer of Zurich's Dolder Grand.

long_biography.plain_text:
At the Dolder Grand, financier Urs Schwarzenbach made his art collection part of a working hotel. He acquired paintings and sculptures over several decades before choosing to display them throughout its public spaces. Works by Andy Warhol and Joan Miró sit alongside a changing selection, allowing visitors to encounter the collection beyond a conventional gallery.

He also established the Black Bears polo team and supported showjumper Steve Guerdat. Schwarzenbach bought Nino des Buissonnets and made the horse available to Guerdat, who won individual Olympic gold in London. For a decade, the rider trained at Schwarzenbach's Swiss stable before acquiring his own premises.
